**Question.** Does a fixed Hq12/Hkv1/D256/top-k2051 FlashInfer CUTE fork beat the pinned vLLM QSA sparse-prefill stage on GB10?

| setup | |
| --- | --- |
| node | `gx10-5e36`, one GB10 |
| kernel | 6.17.13-rocket64k, 64 KiB |
| Rocket code | `6075397e5c930a5bdca1d1d1461db10d28dd2216` |
| vLLM control | `8e685d198`, Apache-2.0 |
| FlashInfer source | `91bda04c66f7cb851e1ab3b78b9fecea644b9844`, Apache-2.0 |
| FlashInfer source SHA-256 | `cfdee49ee968868dee7ce1a0b4e2b62a79e2af8990a3961178388d209627a32f` |
| artifact SHA-256 | `c5f0e70ede9ff571e81c46a3ea80f7a79832135fc7f471de706d06a0fc5b9d33` |

```bash
set -euo pipefail
curve_container=rocket-qsa-prefill-fixedmeta-curve-6075397-01
curve_artifact=/var/tmp/qwen38-qsa-prefill-fixedmeta-curve-6075397-20260908.txt
cleanup_curve() { docker rm -f "$curve_container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
trap cleanup_curve EXIT INT TERM
docker run --rm --name "$curve_container" --gpus all --ipc host --network none \
  --entrypoint bash -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  -v /home/glwillen/Development/rocket-attention-worktree:/rocket:ro \
  -w /rocket vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next -lc \
  'set -euo pipefail; for t in 300 8192; do for c in 1 2 4 8 16; do
    python3 scripts/kernels/qwen38-qsa-prefill-cute.py "$c" "$t" --pattern overlap
  done; done' | tee "$curve_artifact"
```

The p95 ceiling below is the maximum of seven samples. Throughput counts input tokens through this QSA stage. Scaling efficiency is `aggregate(c) / (c * aggregate(c1))`.

| tokens | c | p50 | p95 ceiling | stddev | aggregate | per stream | scaling efficiency |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 300 | 1 | 0.698336 ms | 0.700384 ms | 0.001925 ms | 429,593 tok/s | 429,593 tok/s | 100.0% |
| 300 | 2 | 1.134176 ms | 1.139520 ms | 0.002380 ms | 529,018 tok/s | 264,509 tok/s | 61.57% |
| 300 | 4 | 1.610240 ms | 1.816608 ms | 0.078766 ms | 745,231 tok/s | 186,308 tok/s | 43.37% |
| 300 | 8 | 2.432480 ms | 2.857664 ms | 0.168187 ms | 986,647 tok/s | 123,331 tok/s | 28.71% |
| 300 | 16 | 4.809440 ms | 4.868960 ms | 0.022612 ms | 998,037 tok/s | 62,377 tok/s | 14.52% |
| 8192 | 1 | 6.352736 ms | 6.847904 ms | 0.227165 ms | 1,289,523 tok/s | 1,289,523 tok/s | 100.0% |
| 8192 | 2 | 12.275424 ms | 12.884192 ms | 0.304106 ms | 1,334,699 tok/s | 667,350 tok/s | 51.75% |
| 8192 | 4 | 23.954111 ms | 24.521761 ms | 0.285025 ms | 1,367,949 tok/s | 341,987 tok/s | 26.52% |
| 8192 | 8 | 48.150272 ms | 49.463585 ms | 0.823676 ms | 1,361,072 tok/s | 170,134 tok/s | 13.19% |
| 8192 | 16 | 96.012611 ms | 96.858658 ms | 0.430114 ms | 1,365,154 tok/s | 85,322 tok/s | 6.62% |

| c1 shape | Rocket p50 | matched vLLM p50 | speedup | max abs | mean abs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 300 tokens after an 8192-token prefix | 0.698336 ms | 0.878752 ms | 1.258x | 0.000033379 | 0.000004676 |
| 8192-token prefix | 6.352736 ms | 16.035200 ms | 2.524x | 0.000976562 | 0.000003991 |

All ten shapes returned `graph_exact=true` and `state_unchanged=true`. The 300-token maximum error was at most `0.000033379`; the 8192-token maximum was `0.000976562`. The c4 and c8 300-token rows contained isolated high samples. Their seven-sample coefficients of variation were 4.89% and 6.91%.

The earlier kernel wrote only 16 of 256 output dimensions. The fork now uses an independent D256 output coordinate tensor. Fixed tile geometry, an 8208-wide caller-owned workspace, and builder-side N16 tail finalization removed the per-call allocation and full-workspace sanitization path. The captured graph contains metadata construction and attention on one caller stream.

**Verdict.** Accepted for the QSA sparse-prefill component. The c1 matched comparisons pass output, immutable-state, graph replay, and value gates at both prompt anchors. c2 through c16 have matched-vLLM numerical controls but no matched-vLLM timing. These rates do not measure whole prefill or generated-token throughput.

**Next.**

- Integrate the selected component with QSA state publication and the full prefill graph.
- Measure matched-vLLM prefill latency across c2 through c16.
- Measure end-to-end quality-accepted prefill and decode across the concurrency curve.

**Reopen if.**

- A newer SM121 FlashInfer, vLLM, or CUDA compiler release changes either c1 matched control by more than the seven-sample variance above.
